section_summary: The section concludes a Japanese five-year economic rehabilitation plan, emphasizing exports, foreign aid, capital formation, and economic controls. It then contains an Occupation survey of public interest in purchasing Zaibatsu stocks, State Department memoranda on industrial deconcentration and administration of aid, and a British assessment of Japan’s economic prospects.

subfiles.title: Five-Year Economic Rehabilitation Plan, concluding sections
subfiles.about: Concluding sections discuss trade, aid, capital formation, and requirements for a self-supporting Japanese economy by 1953.
subfiles.summary: The plan expects expanded Asian trade but warns that dollar shortages and inconvertible currencies could obstruct recovery. It calls for high levels of saving and investment, effective use of aid and counterpart funds, export promotion, financial controls, and population measures. Its conclusion stresses that implementation depends on government action and public cooperation.

subfiles.title: The Purchase of Zaibatsu Stocks: An Appraisal of Public Interest
subfiles.doc_type: public opinion survey report; enclosure to despatch 671
subfiles.from: GHQ Civil Information and Education Section, Public Opinion and Sociological Research Division
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A nationwide survey examines public knowledge, ownership, interest, and purchase intentions concerning Zaibatsu stocks.
subfiles.summary: Interviews with more than 5,000 adults found limited understanding of securities democratization and little immediate intent to purchase stocks. About 12 percent owned stocks, while only about 3 percent had a high intention to buy. Experience, knowledge, income, and education were associated with greater receptivity; appendices explain the survey method and estimate changes in stock ownership.

subfiles.title: Attached Airgram
subfiles.about: Proposes revised airgram language distinguishing efficient concentration of production from concentration of ownership.
subfiles.summary: Fearey urges language that supports efficient production while clarifying its relationship to industrial deconcentration.

subfiles.title: Tokyo’s 669 of September 26, 1949
subfiles.about: Comments on Japan’s Five-Year Plan and its political reception.
subfiles.summary: Carwell describes the plan’s goals, Yoshida’s objections, and its reliance on future currency convertibility.

subfiles.title: Attached: ECA Take-Over Proposals
subfiles.about: Submits revised proposals for interdepartmental discussion of ECA administration of Japanese recovery aid.
subfiles.summary: Transmits proposed correspondence and discusses the timing and implications of an ECA takeover.

subfiles.title: Operation of Japanese Recovery Program by the Economic Cooperation Administration
subfiles.about: Recommends prompt agreement on whether ECA should administer U.S. procurement funds for Japanese recovery.
subfiles.summary: The proposal would transfer Washington procurement functions to ECA and establish ECA representation within SCAP in Japan. It argues that these arrangements could improve coordination and advice without changing the existing authority of SCAP or the international control regime.

subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram on Japanese Economic Issues
subfiles.about: Reports on tobacco policy and disappointing trade with Korea, among other economic matters.
subfiles.summary: The damaged OCR preserves discussion of a tobacco monopoly proposal, the Shoup Mission’s tax recommendations, and Korean trade. It says Japanese purchases of Korean products lagged behind plans.

subfiles.title: Brief Summary of Major Japanese Economic Problems Prepared by British Minister (Commercial)
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards and comments on a British commercial minister’s assessment of Japan’s economy.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines Lingeman’s treatment of food, resources, production, trade, inflation, and aid. It notes his disagreement with optimistic trade projections and his view that Japan would likely need substantial U.S. assistance beyond 1953.

subfiles.title: A Bird’s Eye View of Japan’s Major Economic Problems
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s population, food supply, natural resources, industrial production, and foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: The report describes population growth and food shortages, including dependence on imports and U.S. aid. It surveys lost access to former sources of food and raw materials, limited domestic resources, and rising industrial output. The enclosure continues beyond page 215.
